## `Accordion`

type alias in `choscorui::prelude::Accordion`

```rust
pub type Accordion = Configured<Accordion>;
```

Stacked sections of (title, content); `open` edits the open sections.

#### Examples

```rust
struct Faq;

impl View for Faq {
    fn body(&self, cx: &mut Cx) -> impl View {
        let open = cx.state(Vec::new());
        let items = vec![("Shipping".to_owned(), "Two to five days.".to_owned())];
        Accordion::new("Questions", items, open.binding())
    }
}
```

Modifiers: every [`ViewExt`](modifiers.md#viewext) method applies to this view.

### Methods

#### `Accordion::new`

```rust
pub fn new<M>(name: impl IntoLive<TextContent, M>, items: impl Items<(String, String)>, open: Binding<Vec<usize>>) -> Self
```

An accordion named `name` of (title, content) sections.

## `AvatarGroup`

type alias in `choscorui::prelude::AvatarGroup`

```rust
pub type AvatarGroup = Configured<AvatarGroup>;
```

Overlapping avatars named `name`, for example the members of a team.
Use `.with(|group| group.with_count("+3"))` for a count after them and
`.with(|group| group.with_size(size))` for their size.

```rust

fn team() -> impl View {
    AvatarGroup::new(

}
```

## `ButtonGroup`

type alias in `choscorui::prelude::ButtonGroup`

```rust
pub type ButtonGroup = Configured<HostedButtonGroup>;
```

Joined members of a `controls::ButtonGroup`: toggles, buttons,
separators, and text parts. `name` names the group, `labels` names
each member, and `checked`
edits the indices of the checked toggle members. A button member
reports its index through `.on_item`.

#### Examples

```rust
struct Styles;

impl View for Styles {
    fn body(&self, cx: &mut Cx) -> impl View {
        let checked = cx.state(Vec::new());
        let members = vec![
            ButtonGroupMember::Toggle(CommandId(1)),
            ButtonGroupMember::Toggle(CommandId(2)),
        ];
        let group = controls::ButtonGroup::from_members(members, false);
        let labels = vec!["Bold".to_owned(), "Italic".to_owned()];
        ButtonGroup::new("Style", group, labels, checked.binding())
    }
}
```

Modifiers: every [`ViewExt`](modifiers.md#viewext) method applies to this view.

### Methods

#### `ButtonGroup::new`

```rust
pub fn new<M>(name: impl IntoLive<TextContent, M>, group: ButtonGroup, labels: impl Items<String>, checked: Binding<Vec<usize>>) -> Self
```

A view of `group` named `name`, with `labels` for its members and
`checked` for its toggles.

## `ColorPicker`

type alias in `choscorui::prelude::ColorPicker`

```rust
pub type ColorPicker = Configured<ColorPicker>;
```

A color picker: a swatch and hue, saturation, value, and alpha
strips. `hex` edits the color as `#RRGGBB` text, or `#RRGGBBAA` when
the color is not opaque; the picker takes `#RGB` too. Accepting the
color runs `.on_activate`.

#### Examples

```rust
struct Accent;

impl View for Accent {
    fn body(&self, cx: &mut Cx) -> impl View {
        let hex = cx.state("#3366FF".to_owned());
        ColorPicker::new("Accent color", hex.binding())
    }
}
```

Modifiers: every [`ViewExt`](modifiers.md#viewext) method applies to this view.

### Methods

#### `ColorPicker::new`

```rust
pub fn new<M>(name: impl IntoLive<TextContent, M>, hex: Binding<String>) -> Self
```

A color picker named `name` that edits `hex`.

#### `ColorPicker::on_channels`

```rust
pub fn on_channels(self, action: impl Fn([f64; 4]) + 'static) -> Self
```

Runs `action` with the hue, saturation, value, and alpha after
each change by the user, each as a fraction of its range. It also
runs when the hex text stays the same, for example for a new hue
of a gray.

type alias in `choscorui::prelude::DateTimeEdit`

```rust
        DateTimeEdit::new("Start", DateTimeKind::DateTime, start.binding())
```

## `Dial`

type alias in `choscorui::prelude::Dial`

```rust
pub type Dial = Configured<HostedDial>;
```

A rotary control that edits `value`. Like a slider, it covers
`0..=100` with a step of 1 and a page of 10 until `.range`, `.step`,
and `.page` change them. A `.wrapping(true)` dial, such as a compass,
turns past its maximum to its minimum.

#### Examples

```rust
use choscorui_compose::view::{Cx, Dial, View};

struct Heading;

impl View for Heading {
    fn body(&self, cx: &mut Cx) -> impl View {
        let degrees = cx.state(90);
        Dial::new("Heading", degrees.binding()).range(0..=359).wrapping(true)
    }
}
```

Modifiers: every [`ViewExt`](modifiers.md#viewext) method applies to this view.

### Methods

#### `Dial::new`

```rust
pub fn new<M>(name: impl IntoLive<TextContent, M>, value: Binding<i32>) -> Self
```

A dial named `name` that edits `value`.

#### `Dial::page`

```rust
pub fn page(self, page: u32) -> Self
```

The change of one page key. A page of zero becomes 1 and
reports a `ViewError::Clamped`.

#### `Dial::range`

```rust
pub fn range(self, bounds: RangeInclusive<i32>) -> Self
```

The bounds of the value. Reversed bounds become
`start..=start` and report a
`ViewError::Clamped` when the
view mounts.

#### `Dial::step`

```rust
pub fn step(self, step: u32) -> Self
```

The change of one arrow key. A step of zero becomes 1 and
reports a `ViewError::Clamped`.

#### `Dial::wrapping`

```rust
pub fn wrapping(self, wrapping: bool) -> Self
```

Turns past the maximum to the minimum, and back.

### Methods

#### `Input::email`

```rust
pub fn email<M>(name: impl IntoLive<TextContent, M>, value: Binding<String>) -> Self
```

An input for an email address. Return and blur mark text that is
no email address invalid.

#### `Input::filter`

```rust
pub fn filter(self, class: CharClass) -> Self
```

Allows only the characters of `class`. A key or a paste with
another character changes nothing and beeps.

#### `Input::masked`

```rust
pub fn masked<M>(name: impl IntoLive<TextContent, M>, mask: InputMask, value: Binding<String>) -> Self
```

An input that fits what the user types into `mask` and shows its
literals. `value` edits the text with the literals, for example
`(090) 512-3456`. A key that fits no slot changes nothing and
beeps. A paste keeps the characters that fit. The caret keeps its
place among the typed characters, and a deletion of a literal
deletes the typed character before it. Check the value with
`InputMask::validate`.

##### Examples

```rust
struct Phone;

impl View for Phone {
    fn body(&self, cx: &mut Cx) -> impl View {
        let phone = cx.state(String::new());
        let mask = InputMask::parse("(000) 000-0000").expect("a valid mask");
        Input::masked("Phone", mask, phone.binding())
    }
}
```

#### `Input::max_length`

```rust
pub fn max_length(self, length: usize) -> Self
```

Allows at most `length` grapheme clusters. A paste longer than the
room left is cut to the room, and a key with no room beeps.

#### `Input::new`

```rust
pub fn new<M>(name: impl IntoLive<TextContent, M>, value: Binding<String>) -> Self
```

An input named `name` that edits `value`.

#### `Input::number`

```rust
pub fn number<M>(name: impl IntoLive<TextContent, M>, value: Binding<String>) -> Self
```

An input for a number. It takes digits, one leading minus, and one
`.` only.

#### `Input::password`


An input that hides what the user types. Cut and copy do nothing

#### `Input::search`

```rust

```

An input for a search query.

#### `Input::tel`


An input for a phone number. It takes digits, spaces, and

#### `Input::url`

An input for a web address, such as `https://example.com`. Return


## `List`

type alias in `choscorui::prelude::List`

```rust
pub type List = Configured<ItemView>;
```

The rows of the model that `model` makes, one line of text each;
`selection` edits the positions of the selected rows. The list is
virtualized: it paints only the rows in view, so its cost does not
grow with the model. The row height comes from the `ListView` recipe.

#### Examples

```rust
struct Fruits;

impl View for Fruits {
    fn body(&self, cx: &mut Cx) -> impl View {
        let selection = cx.state(Vec::new());
        let model = || Box::new(StringListModel::from_strings(["Apple", "Pear"])) as Box<dyn ItemModel>;
        List::new("Fruits", model, selection.binding())
    }
}
```

Modifiers: every [`ViewExt`](modifiers.md#viewext) method applies to this view.

### Methods

#### `List::new`

```rust
pub fn new<M>(name: impl IntoLive<TextContent, M>, model: impl Fn() -> Box<dyn ItemModel> + 'static, selection: Binding<Vec<usize>>) -> Self
```

A list named `name` of the model that `model` makes.

#### `List::selection_mode`

```rust
pub fn selection_mode(self, mode: SelectionMode) -> Self
```

How many rows the user can select; the default is
`SelectionMode::Extended`.

#### `List::table`

```rust
pub fn table<M>(name: impl IntoLive<TextContent, M>, model: impl Fn() -> Box<dyn ItemModel> + 'static, selection: Binding<Vec<usize>>) -> Self
```

The rows of the model that `model` makes as a table, one cell for
each column; `selection` edits the positions of the selected rows.
Like [`List::new`](#list), the table paints only the rows in
view. Add footer rows and a caption with `.with` and
`ItemView::with_footer` and `ItemView::with_caption`.

type alias in `choscorui::prelude::RangeSlider`

Low and high values along one track; `values` edits both. It covers

```rust
impl View for Price {
    fn body(&self, cx: &mut Cx) -> impl View {
        let price = cx.state((20.0, 80.0));
        RangeSlider::new("Price", price.binding()).range(0.0..=200.0).step(5.0)
    }
}
```


```rust

```

The bounds of both values. Reversed bounds become `start..=start`,
and bounds that are not finite stay as they are. Both report a
`ViewError::Clamped`.

#### `RangeSlider::step`

```rust

```
